judgment.rationale: The stack proves a WPF binding failure during system-theme resource invalidation, but not the PowerToys visual, property, or framework ownership that must change.
evidence: The report stack reaches BindingExpression.SetupDefaultValueConverter, StyleHelper.GetDataTriggerValue, and WPF ThemeManager.OnSystemThemeChanged.
The current issue is on 0.100.2 and has Needs-Author-Feedback.
The triage discussion identifies prior stack-matched reports.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a current diagnostic and trigger matrix while retaining the exact-stack investigation design.

fix_assessment.rationale: Only a red, evidence-gathering design is defensible; no product change should be implemented until the failing WPF target is identified.

proposed_fixes.title: Identify the failing PowerToys Run theme binding before changing behavior
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Provisional: WPF reevaluates a style DataTrigger or resource binding during a system-theme update and throws NullReferenceException; the failing PowerToys target is unknown.
plan: Capture a fresh trace after reproduction with Run visibility and display/theme transition recorded.
Enable binding diagnostics or instrument the PowerLauncher theme-update path to identify the FrameworkElement, DependencyProperty, and XAML resource.
Rewrite only a proven PowerToys binding or, with maintainer approval, consider an exact-stack nonfatal classification after confirming UI health.
verification: The trace identifies a specific binding or establishes a framework-owned failure before any code change.
Any approved mitigation must preserve Run rendering and continue reporting unrelated UI exceptions.

confidence.rationale: The WPF stack is precise about timing but does not identify the application binding that failed.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run reports a WPF NullReferenceException while WPF refreshes theme resources, without identifying the failing application binding.
known_information: The report is from PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows build 26200.
The stack includes WPF binding, style, resource dictionary, and ThemeManager frames.
Similar stack reports are referenced by triage.
inferences: The failure may be framework-owned or in a PowerLauncher style/resource binding.
Suppressing the report without proving UI health could conceal corruption.
issue_context.analysis: The generic WPF stack cannot distinguish a faulty PowerToys template from a runtime defect. Collection must name the binding before a product fix is selected.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue stack, triage duplicate references, and fork mirror 643.
Candidate areas are PowerLauncher theme management, XAML triggers, and exception classification.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic captured immediately after reproduction plus the exact trigger matrix
information_gaps.why_needed: It is needed to identify the WPF target and distinguish theme, high-contrast, sleep, dock, and visibility paths.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the current stable build, reproduce once, add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward, and report light/dark, high-contrast, sleep/hibernate, dock/undock, and Run visible/hidden results.

design.root_cause: Not established; an application DataTrigger or resource binding is a candidate only.
evidence: [Observed] WPF throws during SetupDefaultValueConverter while ThemeManager updates resources.
[Observed] The report does not name a FrameworkElement or DependencyProperty.
[Inferred] A target-specific rewrite is safer than broad exception suppression.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Theme invalidation causes WPF to reevaluate bindings without exposing the failing target in the report.
implementation_steps.change: Collect target-level binding evidence, then change only the proven binding to a theme-safe mechanism.
implementation_steps.code_block: Theme transition -> capture FrameworkElement, DependencyProperty, and resource key -> reproduce -> replace only the failing binding.
edge_cases: Cover high contrast and rapid preference changes.
tests: Manual target-specific theme regression after identification.

verify: Reproduce the exact stack on current and affected builds.
After a targeted change, repeat theme, high-contrast, sleep, and dock transitions with Run visible and hidden.
Confirm unrelated UI exceptions remain reportable.
risks: Broad NullReferenceException suppression can mask broken UI.
Speculative XAML changes can churn unrelated templates.
alternatives: Wait for runtime servicing if diagnostics establish framework ownership.
Use exact-stack mitigation only after approval and UI-health proof.

adversary.verdict: Blocking objection remains: ownership and the failing binding are unproven.
adversary.notes: Do not implement a speculative product fix.

comment.body: The reported stack narrows the failure to WPF binding evaluation during a system-theme resource update, but it does not identify the failing PowerToys control or show whether the runtime owns it. Please reproduce once on the current stable build, add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward, and report results for light/dark and high-contrast changes, sleep/hibernate, dock/undock, and with PowerToys Run visible versus hidden.
